clue.text: Telephotographic picture unlikely to succeed

definitions.meaning: a photograph or film frame taken from far away, often with a telephoto lens
a bet, entrant or venture with only a slim chance of winning

explanation.surface: A photo taken through a telephoto lens is not expected to come out well.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one phrase: a distant camera view, and an outsider with small odds of winning.

clue.text: Bent over to give heed to press boss

parts.note: list is an old word for listen or pay attention
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone leaned in to pay attention to a newspaper chief.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship that lists leans to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that has listed has leaned or tilted to one side.

clue.text: Raised firearm to obtain a piece of gold

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a gun is a firearm
to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: A prospector lifts a weapon to grab a lump of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump of precious metal found naturally, as panned by prospectors.

clue.text: Fall ill when neck is dislocated

indicators.note: dislocated means put out of place, so the letters of neck is are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone becomes unwell after putting their neck out.
explanation.definitionFit: To become sick, to start to feel unwell.

clue.text: Not inclined to be honest

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to be truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both horizontal, without tilt, and trustworthy in one's dealings.

clue.text: Illegal acts by a part of the Ukraine

parts.note: crime is the collective word for unlawful acts

explanation.surface: Lawbreaking carried out by one region of Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula on the Black Sea is a region historically belonging to Ukraine.

clue.text: Easily understood how to make bread and ale

indicators.note: how to make suggests a recipe, with the letters of the two items mixed together into a new form

explanation.surface: Clear instructions for baking a loaf and brewing beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing that is clear and legible can be followed without difficulty.

clue.text: Michael about to declare his views are unorthodox

definitions.note: a clause describing a person; the answer is the noun for such a person

indicators.note: about means the short form of Michael goes around the other piece

parts.note: Mick is a familiar form of the name Michael
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Michael is on the point of announcing that his opinions are unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tempts the solver to read 'about to declare' as one phrase, but it is the container signal for the name round the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent-minded nonconformist is someone whose opinions break from convention.

clue.text: But in Austria turgid talk is not the norm

definitions.note: a phrase; the answer is the matching adjective, departing from the norm

parts.note: aber is the German for but, the language of Austria
a rant is bombastic, overblown speech

explanation.surface: Yet in Vienna pompous speeches are unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deviating from the usual standard is abnormal.

clue.text: Returning fuel supply to a conurbation requires foresight

indicators.note: returning means the word for fuel is read backwards, coming back the way it went

parts.note: gas is a common fuel for heating and cooking
a conurbation is a large built-up urban area, a city

explanation.surface: Bringing energy supplies back to a big urban area calls for careful planning.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom and shrewd judgement include the ability to see ahead, so foresight is a near synonym.

clue.text: A Ravel composition anglers consider gentle

definitions.note: a gentle is a maggot used as bait; the answer is plural, the clue word singular

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of the composer's name are put together afresh

explanation.surface: Fishermen regard a piece by the French composer Ravel as soft and mild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gentle' reads as an adjective, but anglers use it as a noun: a gentle is a blowfly maggot, a fly's young form, used as bait.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentles are blowfly maggots, the young grub stage of insects, which anglers put on hooks as bait.

clue.text: Explanations for wild geese in sex change

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged birds are placed inside the other scrambled word
change here means the three letters of the word sex are rearranged
wild means the letters of the birds' name are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Interpretations offered for wild geese undergoing a sex change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' and 'change' are separate anagram signals, one for each word, and 'in' sets the scrambled birds between the second and third letters of the scrambled other word.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of exegesis, a critical interpretation of a text, especially scripture.

clue.text: More beautiful, but that's just comparative

definitions.meaning: the comparative form of just, meaning more even-handed

explanation.surface: Someone claims a person is better-looking, but only by comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both prettier and more impartial, the comparative of two senses of fair.

clue.text: Made a monk get things straight

definitions.meaning: placed someone in a religious community

explanation.surface: Joining a monastery helped someone sort their life out.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally entered into a religious brotherhood, and also arranged neatly or sorted.

clue.text: Noted local owner is antimonarchical

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi)
a local is a British pub, so its owner or landlord is a publican

explanation.surface: A well-known pub landlord is against the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub, whose keeper is a publican.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone favouring a republic rejects rule by kings and queens.

clue.text: Urges a young man to prepare a light meal

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: She encourages a youth to cook a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Urges' reads as a verb but supplies EGGS, from 'egg on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold dish of chopped boiled eggs with mayonnaise makes a simple lunch.

clue.text: Monotonous chant for a service

parts.note: even means unvarying and regular
a chant is a kind of song

explanation.surface: A droning chant fit for a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglican evening prayer is a church service.

clue.text: Award for expert accommodating company junior

indicators.note: accommodating means the expert word houses the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an ace is a highly skilled person
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: A prize for a skilled person who takes on a young trainee in the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour or token of praise given in recognition.

clue.text: Admit indebtedness and don't demand cash

definitions.meaning: acknowledge what one owes to another, as in praise or thanks
let a customer buy now and pay later

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to owing money and tells a creditor not to insist on payment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both acknowledging merit owed to someone and selling on deferred payment terms.

clue.text: A small sea bird following the ship

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tern is a sea bird

explanation.surface: A little gull trails behind a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical word for behind or at the back of a vessel.

clue.text: Where to find the last seven letters of pudding

parts.note: the letters are located following a point in the alphabet, so the place is after
the final seven letters of the alphabet, T to Z, all follow S, the letter they come after

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where the end of the word pudding is found.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites counting letters in 'pudding', but the alphabet is meant: its last seven letters, T to Z, come after S, so the phrase is read as AFTER S. The answer is British slang for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for the sweet course served after the main dish.

clue.text: Excess nut found in cereal grains

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase; the answer is the substance so described

parts.note: a glut is an oversupply
printers call an en space a nut

explanation.surface: Too many nuts turned up among the grain crops.
explanation.walkthrough: Typesetters say 'nut' for an en so it is not confused with an em.
explanation.definitionFit: A protein present in wheat, barley and rye.

clue.text: Forward child about to reach a conclusion

indicators.note: about means the child word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a son is a male child
to end is to come to a close

explanation.surface: A precocious youngster is on the point of finishing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter or parcel is to dispatch it onward to a new address.

clue.text: Egotistic ex-student mirrored variety of faults

indicators.note: mirrored means the two letters appear back to front, as in a mirror

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: a variety of means the letters of faults are mixed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A self-centred old boy reflected on his many failings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mirrored' turns OB into BO, and 'variety of' rearranges FAULTS as ASTFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vain and self-centred tends to brag about themselves.

clue.text: Simpleton taken aback by a hard scrubber

indicators.note: taken aback is read literally as taken backwards, so the word is spelt in reverse

parts.note: a fool is a silly or simple person
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A dim-witted person is startled by a tough cleaning tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise but turns FOOL into LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried fibrous pod of a gourd is used as a bath sponge for rubbing the skin.

clue.text: He sticks to a woman sunk in depression

indicators.note: sunk in means the woman piece is lowered inside the hollow word

parts.note: a dent is a hollow pressed into a surface
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A man stays loyal to a woman who is deep in low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests gloom but is a physical hollow, DENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or follower is someone who stays attached to a cause or leader.

clue.text: Pick of the Australian army!

definitions.meaning: a pick is a tool for breaking ground, one that excavates
a soldier from Australia or New Zealand, especially of the world wars

explanation.surface: The best of Australia's soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick is an excavating tool, and Australian soldiers have long been nicknamed for trench work.

clue.text: Thousands staked by scion of the family

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
money staked on a horse is bet on it

explanation.surface: Big sums wagered by the heir to a wealthy dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's son is a descendant, a young member of the line.
